title: Hall Chicken Noodle Soup
seoTitle: Hall Chicken Noodle Soup | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Classic chicken noodle soup with egg noodles for ten
subtitle: Classic chicken noodle soup with egg noodles for ten
description: Chicken thighs simmer with mirepoix and herbs until tender, then shred into a rich broth with egg noodles and carrots. Simple, restorative, and built for the biggest stock pot in the hall.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Hall Chicken Noodle Soup in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Poach the chicken
steps.instruction: Simmer chicken thighs in broth with onion, bay leaves, and thyme 30–35 minutes until internal temp reaches 165°F and meat pulls easily from bone. Target oven/smoker temperature: 165°F.

steps.title: Shred and strain
steps.instruction: Remove chicken, shred meat, discard skin and bones. Strain broth if cloudy, return to pot, and skim excess fat. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Build the soup base
steps.instruction: Add carrots, celery, and garlic to broth. Simmer 15 minutes until vegetables tender. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cook noodles separately
steps.instruction: Boil egg noodles in salted water until al dente, about 7 minutes. Drain and toss with a little oil. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Hall Chicken Noodle Soup onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Ladle and garnish
steps.instruction: Return shredded chicken to soup. Season with salt and pepper. Portion noodles into bowls, ladle hot soup over, and garnish with parsley.

proTips: A splash of lemon juice at service brightens heavy broth instantly.
Turmeric pinch adds golden color without changing the classic flavor.
Freeze half the shredded chicken and broth base separately for fast future soup.
tonightSpread: Soup with saltine crackers and buttered bread on the side.
Simple green salad for crew who want crunch alongside the bowl.
leftovers: Store noodles separate from broth or they absorb everything overnight.
Reduce broth and add cream for a quick chicken pot pie filling.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Chicken noodle soup is the universal reset meal. It reheats perfectly, fills the hall with comfort smell, and nobody complains when they are tired or under the weather.
mealPrepNotes: Poach thighs gently—boiling toughens meat. Cook noodles separately and add at service so they do not bloat in the pot. Skim fat from broth for cleaner flavor.
